pullRequests.body:
Contributors currently have only a short setup paragraph and no concrete path from a first PR to independent maintainer duties. This adds a clean-clone/disposable-data guide, architecture-to-task map, maintained starter proposals, consent-based role/access and succession records, and a security/release tabletop runbook for #576.

The serial maintainer drill reuses existing release guards and real archive/restore fixture suites. It isolates child runtime/credential settings, requires clean unchanged source and completed assertions, and retains exact commands, raw output and SHA-256 receipts, including failed subprocess recovery reports. Partial mode exits 1. A read-only verifier checks retained/copied bundles against a separately supplied source SHA/version, raw report counts, exact commands/suites, digests, sizes and explicit human/release gaps. It never executes recorded commands or opens embedded paths, and reads earlier v1 bundles across OS path formats. Windows dotted-worktree selection uses a root-relative match plus exact-file/result validation.

Validation on Windows x64 / Node 22.13.1 / npm 11.19.0:

- Fresh `npm ci --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund` and `npm run test:dependencies` passed in the owned checkout.
- `node --test scripts/maintainer-drill.test.mjs`: 13 passed, no skips. Includes corrupt/copied evidence, stale identity, fabricated counts, changed commands, linked files, failed report retention and cross-platform path cases.
- Focused ESLint for both new scripts with `--max-warnings=0`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `node scripts/maintainer-drill.mjs` at `0468cbd2668256c39d8a43b88cd4b3ecdfac9fe9`: 28 release guards plus 51 recovery assertions in four suites passed, no skips, source clean before/after. Receipt SHA-256: `55c9738e1260aaf3e5698a759bd0e73630b1e0f8ed14f48739fdd39d1142fabb`. Raw receipt/output is retained locally for coordinator evidence integration.
- Actual read-only verification CLI passed on the retained current bundle and the earlier `7acc3f35` v1 bundle against their independently specified revisions/version. Real `--release-only` mode returned partial/exit 1.

Scope limits: release guards use mocked subprocesses; recovery suites use synthetic files/mocked service boundaries. Local full builds, consumer-installed release, upgrade, real account-access recovery, human-operated drill, private triage tabletop and sustained human observations remain pending. Hashes establish consistency, not runner signatures or human independence. Prior revision CI passed both OS builds, typecheck, lint, isolated tests and release safety; its ordinary tests were still running when the follow-up was pushed. Current-head CI must qualify the current revision separately. Proposed human targets still need #564 agreement, consenting independent humans, owner-approved recruitment/access, actual 90-day observations and external reassessment. No humans/permissions are invented and #576 remains open. Engineering #565 owns workflow adoption/enforcement; Security owns SECURITY.md; Production #570 owns qualified installed recovery recipes.

Refs #576; contributes source evidence to #563.

pullRequests.body:
When an MCP disconnect returns success or a disabled server reports disconnected, operators cannot tell whether FLUJO observed its managed stdio child exit. The close helper also previously treated a missing child as exited. This change returns and retains a redacted version 1 receipt keyed to workspace, runtime ID and generation, with explicit observed/unknown/not-applicable outcomes, forced escalation, elapsed time and bounded error classification.

Concurrent/repeated disconnects share the same receipt, including across asynchronous config reads. Disconnect waits for an already pending connect, and replacement connects invalidate prior receipt qualification. Status and lifecycle diagnostics expose the current receipt; application-wide disconnect returns per-server receipts separately from its legacy connection outcome lists. The operator contract explains that child exit does not certify descendants, remote cleanup, billing, business drain or live admission.

Refs #547, #570, #563. This is the first Production-readiness slice; it does not close those issues or claim A- readiness.

Validation in the owned Windows checkout, Node v22.13.1, Next 16.3.5, base 3511ba49514fe8cf525f5a22c16c3806bf3886ba:

- Four focused suites pass (46 tests): real disposable graceful/forced child exits, unresolved exit, SDK-close failure, overlapping/repeated disconnects, pending-connect ordering, stale generations, workspace-scoped bookkeeping, redaction, status serialization, unrelated-process preservation and equivalent runtime-key escaping.
- Six adjacent reconnect/OAuth/status regression suites pass (29 tests).
- Root `npm run typecheck`, scoped ESLint with `--max-warnings=0`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Checkout-local dependency validation passes after `npm ci --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund`.

The targeted Jest commands use `--testMatch '**/__tests__/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}' --runTestsByPath` because the default managed-Windows `<rootDir>` glob produces mixed slash escaping and discovers no tests. No production runner configuration was changed.

Pending acceptance: coordinator-approved Windows/Linux builds and CI; Linux process witnesses; exact installed npm/image/installer identity and authenticated operator journey; independent non-author acceptance. Security owns ingress/secret/isolation changes, and #553 retains copied-snapshot scheduler suppression. No release, deployment, merge, live teardown, controller activation or paid provider operation occurred.

The tracked lifecycle coordinator baseline contains one literal NUL separator and no UTF-8 BOM. Its runtime-key string now uses an equivalent textual TypeScript escape (covered by a direct identity assertion). A file-specific .gitattributes diff rule renders the historical NUL-containing source as text, so the logic changes remain reviewable.

pullRequests.body:
The invocation-source contract lived in backend execution state, so the conversation sidebar imported a backend type. Other backend/frontend crossings were undocumented and new crossings had no automated guard. This incremental #571 slice moves the eight source values and classification helpers into a dependency-free shared module, preserving all backend exports, and enforces direct backend/frontend/shared import direction.

The checker resolves declarations with the checkout's TypeScript configuration and rejects new crossings and stale exceptions. Twelve existing declarations remain explicitly documented debt; allowance is tied to the exact importer, target, and declaration, so extending a legacy import or changing a type-only import to a runtime import fails. The normal Jest suite discovers the architecture guard. The architecture guide maps run lifecycle, authority, approvals, subflows, persistence, provider/archive dispatch, cancellation/recovery, and MCP lifecycle ownership, with human maintenance exercises and separate source/media/package/Git size measurements.

Validation at `a3acaea54e50054bc98dc33e421181b1af40a10a`, based on `3511ba49514fe8cf525f5a22c16c3806bf3886ba`, Windows, Node 22.13.1, npm 11.19.0, checkout-local `npm ci --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund`:

- `node scripts/check-import-boundaries.cjs`: 897 files, 12 legacy crossings, zero new crossings or stale allowances.
- `npm run typecheck` and scoped ESLint with `--max-warnings=0`: pass.
- 153 assertions across 15 targeted suites: boundary negative fixtures/compatibility, ordinary and ephemeral runs, unattended drive-forward, origin display, approval/caps, debugger frames, subflow recovery, cancellation/recovery, authority/archive and MCP multiple-instance/teardown regressions.
- An uppercase Windows `BACKEND` import negative control exposed a case-sensitive layer classification gap in the first commit. The follow-up fix uses the resolver's filesystem-casing rule; the new regression and CLI probe now reject the crossing (expected exit 1).
- `git diff --check`: pass.

The existing runner initially reported **no tests found** on this Windows `.codex` worktree path. Targeted runs passed using `--testMatch '**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts' --runTestsByPath <exact paths>` (`jsdom` uses the equivalent component glob). This limitation is retained for Engineering; no runner/workflow configuration was changed here. Both OS builds, typecheck/lint, isolated tests and release safety passed remotely on the earlier `dbf277b6` commit; its full test job was still pending before this correction. Exact-head full Windows/Linux builds, full/isolated CI and packed/installed-artifact acceptance remain gates. No local full build or soak was run while coordinator host capacity was constrained.

This is a direct-layer maintainability check, not transitive client-bundle analysis or process isolation. Auth/crypto, memory/archive behavior, worker/scheduler behavior and live runtimes are unchanged. #571 remains open for sequenced further simplification, an independent human's maintenance exercise, agreed performance evidence, release acceptance and external reassessment. Engineering can invoke the checker explicitly in verification; the tests already integrate without runner edits.

Refs #571, #563. No grade, merge, release or deployment is claimed.

pullRequests.body:
Adds an opt-in owner API bearer boundary for #566 under epic #563. `FLUJO_OWNER_AUTH_FILE` selects a bounded, validated durable policy with hashed random credentials, explicit scopes, expiry and revocation. Proxy ingress and the shared workspace handler independently authenticate before sensitive access; execution-only OpenAI grants cannot reach configuration, approvals, secret-bearing APIs or broad MCP transports. Existing worker/snapshot bearers, narrow trusted execution adapters, state-bound OAuth callbacks and token-authenticated POST webhooks retain separate authority.

Includes the proposed versioned threat/client migration contract and `SECURITY.md`. This is a foundation for review: browser pairing/sessions, established-stream revocation, remaining service coverage, startup refusal, fine-grained MCP/flow grants, private credential migration (#567) and OS/container enforcement (#568) remain open. Existing anonymous localhost behavior remains when the policy is absent. Do not activate the opt-in profile on an existing browser deployment before its migration gate. Independent security review and installed-artifact acceptance are pending; no A- grade, release or public readiness is claimed.

Validation at `2c02fd0d3e4c36e702537a2e67bdd3d240101533` on Windows/Node 22.13.1: the new 36-case admission suite passed, including serial fresh-process policy/revocation/corruption probes; existing ingress/workspace (131) and OAuth (6) regression cases passed. Root typecheck, scoped new-module TypeScript, changed-file ESLint and diff checks passed. Tests used a documented temporary explicit-match config because the stock Windows managed-path glob collected zero tests; Engineering owns the shared fix. MCP typechecks, full suites, production builds, current dependency audit remediation and packed/installed acceptance are pending coordinator capacity or CI. Exact commands, toolchain identity, failed attempts and workaround checksums are in `docs/security/owner-access-v1-evidence.md`.

GitHub private vulnerability reporting was observed disabled; enabling it and naming the responder remain maintainer actions. Related: #566, #567, #568, #101, #527. This PR does not close those issues.

This change requires current-attempt job evidence for the exact main-push SHA, adds a final fail-closed verification check, and makes Ubuntu/Windows packed app/MCP process smoke part of PR verification while retaining completed-assertion and skip accounting.

It also pins direct action dependencies, scopes workflow permission defaults, adds dependency/CodeQL scan configuration and CODEOWNERS routing, and supplies a proposed administrator ruleset, a read-only effective-rule auditor and a disposable merge-denial drill.

- 176 serial Node contract/release tests passed, no failures or skips; scoped ESLint passed; git diff checks passed.
- Earlier installer-inclusive targeted run passed 199 tests; installer fixtures exercised Bash and PowerShell without a real release.
- Fresh dependency audit FAILED: 8 high, 1 critical, 1 moderate affected packages. No exceptions or threshold reductions were added.

The default-setup API was forbidden, Dependabot explicitly disabled, secret-scanning API unavailable. YAML does not establish repository enforcement.
- Security/Code health must coordinate dependency remediation and triage fresh CodeQL findings. Existing stale analysis alerts include critical/high findings.
- Hosted Windows/Linux builds, packed smoke, full ordinary/isolated suites and fresh scanner runs remain pending. No full build/Jest run was started on the capacity-constrained shared host.
- Published-release identities, installed browser/operator acceptance, human security/release tabletop and independent reassessment remain separate gates. Protected-main release preparation must use a reviewed version PR and exact-SHA workflow dispatch; no publisher-bot bypass is proposed.

Contributes to #565 and epic #563; does not close either issue.

pullRequests.body:
Model dispatch completion/error currently inflates and rewrites the entire archived transcript. New v2 dispatches keep canonical/wire/SDK inputs and media references immutable, and persist outcomes in a separate atomic record capped at 1 KiB. Every observed SDK invocation retains its own dispatch ID and attempt ordinal, including retries. Historical v1 archives retain their existing read/update behavior.

The API reader overlays identity-validated outcomes; recovery ZIP validation and the Persona endurance collector understand both versions. Terminal v2 endurance evidence binds snapshot and outcome hashes separately. The versioned compatibility contract is in `docs/performance/model-turn-archive-v2.md`; older readers cannot inspect new v2 archives, so writer/reader pins must move together.

Partial delivery for #569; related to #520. This removes outcome-update transcript allocations only. Initial archive/inspection/media hydration allocations, runtime admission/event/queue budgets, whole-process retained-memory acceptance, original-provider confirmation and A- reassessment remain open.

Validation on Windows / Node 22.13.1:

- Root and all five MCP typechecks pass; changed-file lint and diff checks pass.
- Eight focused Jest suites / 93 tests cover 5.6M canonical characters, 2M wire characters, 1 MiB media, immutable snapshot bytes, bounded metadata, disk failure, legacy compatibility, real loopback SDK HTTP 400/resume, 503 retry and cache negotiation, suspended streaming, capture/deletion authority, recovery capture/restore, capped ephemeral cleanup and HTTP-400 retry classification.
- The full Persona endurance-evidence command passes 35 assertions, including a fresh-process archive reader and separate outcome-hash validation. These are evidence/fixture tests, not a live endurance run.
- A controlled replacement of only the v2 outcome path with the legacy full read/inflate/parse/stringify/gzip/rewrite fails the transcript-read assertion as expected; source restoration was checksum-verified. The eight other tests in that suite are unselected in the negative control only.

The explicit local Jest test glob works around Windows `<rootDir>` expansion under `.codex`; no runner configuration, workload threshold, skip or quarantine is changed. Full default-heap Windows/Linux builds, complete CI/process checks, fresh selected-release Persona soak, installed-artifact journeys and independent/human/live acceptance remain pending. No merge, release, deployment, real-provider call or private runtime mutation was performed.
